headline: SimLife-BP tests long-horizon behavioral-rule inference in synthetic household simulations
summary: Peng et al. present SimLife-BP, a benchmark for inferring symbolic behavioral patterns from long synthetic household timelines. The current v2 paper describes 106 episodes, up to 48.23 hours and 120 in-game days, with 1,439 question-answer pairs; tasks test direct, counterfactual, noisy-counterfactual and inverse reasoning under three hint levels. Across reported model evaluations, performance depends strongly on the evidence pipeline: most vision-plus-language models remain near chance on average question accuracy, while Gemma-4-31B-it reaches 36.2% all-correct and 74.6% question accuracy with full hints over noiseless text-only evidence. The authors also report shortcutting by frequency heuristics and difficulty adapting when patterns change. These are paper-reported results in scripted Sims 4 simulations with deterministic symbolic rules and generated dialogue, not evidence of real human understanding or deployed household-agent performance.
